summary.whatChanges: Zod v4 `prefault` no longer strips `undefined` from its output/default types, and object parsing (runtime, JIT, and compiled codegen) now always emits a key for defaulted properties even when the resolved value is `undefined`. Mini's `prefault` accepts `undefined` defaults. Tests added for classic and mini.
behaviorChanges: Parsing an object with a prefaulted field that resolves to undefined now yields the key present with value undefined instead of omitting it (e.g. `{a: undefined}` rather than `{}`)
`z.prefault(schema, undefined)` / a factory returning undefined is now allowed by the types instead of being rejected by `NoUndefined`
Output type of a prefault schema is now `output<T>` (may include undefined) instead of `NoUndefined<output<T>>`
Same key-preserving behavior applies in jitless, JIT, and `compileFn`/`z.compile` code paths, and inside tuples, lazy, nullable, and readonly wrappers
A prefault wrapped in `.optional()` still drops the key when input is absent
risks: Parsed object shape changed: consumers relying on `Object.keys`, spread, or JSON.stringify of prefaulted fields will see an extra undefined key
Widened prefault output type can introduce new `undefined` in inferred types, causing downstream type errors
Three separate implementations (interpreter `handlePropertyResult`, JIT codegen, compile.ts `mayOmitUndefined`) must stay in sync; divergence would give inconsistent results per execution mode
Tests mutate global `z.config({jitless})` state, which can leak if a test throws outside the try/finally
